scope: Current export-owned package asset routes and streaming carriers

paired.method: Unmodified Source and Native providers consume identical frozen package files; compare status, exact owned headers, body byte count and SHA-256, including 160 KiB multi-chunk images.

verification.native: 22 passed for assets/current resources/registry, underlying exports resolver, generic resource carriers and historical Loader; final 3 asset tests passed after adding actual HTTP disconnect observation.
verification.scope_reason: Covers exact require-condition self-reference exports, exclusions/absence/inactive rows, encoded paths and malformed percent/UTF-8, typed immutable/SVG headers, exact ETag matching, HEAD/304 without file open, all three carriers, cancellation before first pull and after partial consumption, real 8 MiB HTTP disconnect, and cancellation while an executor read remains in flight.

behavior: Assets resolve from the addressed active package through its exports under Node require conditions; file type follows the resolved target, not the request extension.
Only supported image extensions are served, with immutable cache, quoted encoded-path ETag, nosniff and SVG script-src none. Only an exact If-None-Match value yields 304.

Each GET owns an asynchronous file open/read/close sequence. HEAD and 304 create no file body. Closing before first pull still drains and closes the open; in-flight disk reads complete before the descriptor closes.
Current ClientModules registers the canonical Web resource contract, exposing the same async provider through direct Fetch, readResource and HTTP streaming.

A Source pair exposed that a literal malformed percent obtained by decoding %25 must not address an existing filesystem name. The Native route now validates the file-URL decoding boundary and the final pair passes.

cleanup.retained: Initial mismatch and final paired observations, input hashes, commands, logs/XML, compact observations, selected Source report and cleanup/process receipts.

limitations: Targeted completion, not an exhaustive Node CommonJS package resolver qualification. Existing read-only resolver is reused with explicit require conditions.
Official current Web candidate binding/retry follows; no full regression, Portable/browser/Win7 acceptance or upstream promotion is established.
